sections.text:
The tasks you approve, and search over your content, are offered to AI agents too, with the same rules as for people. Agents connect over MCP (Model Context Protocol), the standard way Claude, Cursor and other AI apps use outside tools.
There are two ways to connect:
Over the web: every site with intent0 answers MCP at /intent0/mcp. Use this once your site is online.
On your computer: npx intent0 mcp runs the same tools from your project folder. Use this while you build.
Agents get:
search_site: search Site Memory and get cited sections.
One tool per public, approved task. Tasks that need sign-in stay in the browser.
Takes about two minutes. You need Claude Desktop and Node.js 20 or newer.

In Claude Desktop, open Settings, then Developer, then Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json:
macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json

Paste this into the file. Replace the folder with your website's folder, and the address with where your site runs:
If the file already has other servers, add "my-site" next to them inside mcpServers.
On Windows, if Claude can't start npx, use "command": "cmd" and put "/c", "npx" at the start of args.
Quit Claude Desktop completely (from the tray or menu bar, not only the window) and open it again. Claude reads the config file only when it starts.

Open a new chat and look in the tools menu of the message box: my-site should be listed with search_site and your tasks. Then ask Claude something about your site, for example "Search my-site for getting started". Claude asks your permission the first time it uses a tool.

For a site that is online, run this in your terminal:
While you build, use your project folder instead:

code.code: claude mcp add --transport http my-site https://your-site.com/intent0/mcp
claude mcp add my-site -- npx intent0 mcp --dir . --site http://localhost:3000

sections.text: Run claude mcp list in the terminal, or type /mcp inside Claude Code. my-site should show as connected.
Add the same mcpServers block to .cursor/mcp.json in your project, then open Cursor Settings, then MCP, and check that my-site is switched on.
In browsers that support WebMCP, the Ask layer registers the same tools for agents working in the visitor's own session.

Agents are told exactly which details are missing instead of guessing.
Tasks that can't be undone need confirmed: true, which the agent sends only after asking the person.
Required steps, such as OTP checks, can't be skipped.

The dashboard is where you review what intent0 offers on your site. Run it in your website's folder:
The command prints a link to the Dashboard page on this website. The page connects to the command running on your computer, so your files and your model key never leave your machine. There are no accounts to create.

Switch each task on or off. Visitors and AI agents only get tasks that are switched on.
Approve the manifest, and the "you may also need" notes shown after a task.
Choose the model, test the connection, and replace the API key. The key is saved to .env.local and never shown.
Rebuild Site Memory from your docs and running site.
Changes are written to intent0.manifest.json, intent0.memory.json and .env.local, the same files the CLI uses. Your site picks them up without a restart. A new model needs a server restart.
The dashboard server only listens on your computer (127.0.0.1, port 4200) and needs the token in the printed link. Other websites open in your browser can't use it.

intent0 adds an intent layer to a website you already have. Visitors press Ask this site in the bottom-right corner, type or say what they want, and get a page built for that request: a guided form for a task, or an answer from your own content with its sources.
Nothing about your website changes. intent0 reads your code once, writes down the tasks it found, and only offers the tasks you approve.

A website with a backend (Next.js, Express, Laravel, Django, Flask, Spring, ASP.NET, Go or plain PHP), or a documentation site.
Node.js 20 or newer on the computer where you run the commands.
A model you choose and pay for yourself: a free Groq or NVIDIA key works, and so does a local Ollama model.

Run this in your website's folder:
init does five things:
Reads your routes, forms and API handlers.
Asks which model to use and saves the key to .env.local on your server.
Maps your site into user tasks, such as "apply for a passport" or "track my application".
Shows you the tasks and asks you to approve them.
Builds Site Memory from your docs and pages, then adds the Ask button.
Start your site and press Ask this site in the bottom-right corner, or Ctrl K.

intent0.manifest.json: the approved tasks. Only tasks that are approved and switched on are ever offered.
intent0.memory.json: Site Memory, your content split into sections with links and exact code blocks.
.env.local: your model settings and key. Never sent to the browser.

Besides tasks, intent0 answers questions from your own content: docs, guides, notices and help pages. Every statement links to the page it came from, and code examples are copied exactly from your docs, never written by the model.

Site Memory is the file intent0 answers from. Build it with:
index reads Markdown and MDX files in your repository, and the pages of your running website. It splits them into sections, keeps code blocks whole and records the links between pages. It needs no model.
Private areas are never read: admin, account, profile, settings, login and staff pages are skipped.
Run index again whenever your content changes, or use Rebuild from the site in the dashboard.

--crawl http://localhost:3000: read the site at this address.
--no-crawl: read only the files in the repository.
--max-pages 300: read more pages (the default is 150).
A site with no forms works as an information assistant. Ask "how do I set this up with Vue" and the page shows only the Vue guide, with its exact code.
intent0 uses the model you choose, with your own key, on your own server. The key is never sent to the browser and never written into the manifest.

init offers these presets. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works as custom.
Provider   Model   Notes --- --- --- groq   openai/gpt-oss-120b   Free tier available nvidia   openai/gpt-oss-120b   Free tier available ollama   llama3.2   Runs on your own computer, no key openai   gpt-4.1-mini   Paid custom   any   Any OpenAI-compatible base URL

The settings live in .env.local (settings in .env are used too):
Change them in the dashboard, or pass --provider, --model and --base-url to init.
If no model is set, intent0 still works: tasks use safe forms built from the manifest, and answers are put together from Site Memory without a model.

On a Next.js App Router project, npx intent0 init adds two files and one line:
app/intent0/[action]/route.ts: the server part. It holds your model key and talks to the model.
components/intent0-bar.tsx: the Ask button and the generated pages.
<Intent0Bar /> inside <body> in your root layout.
Pass your own buttons and inputs so generated pages look like the rest of your site:
intent0 uses your site's font. Set the accent colour with a CSS variable:
For PHP, Express, Django, Flask, Spring, ASP.NET, Go or plain HTML sites, intent0 runs as a small server next to your website, and your pages load one script.
serve runs on port 4100. It holds your model key and only answers requests from your website's own address.

code.code:
npx intent0 init
npx intent0 serve

sections.text: Add this to your shared layout or footer, before </body>:

data-lang="hi": answers in Hindi, and voice input listens for Hindi.
data-accent="#0f766e": the accent colour. By default intent0 picks it up from your buttons and links.
data-mount="#some-element": where to add intent0 in the page.
To allow more website addresses, start the server with --origin:
These rules are enforced by code, not by asking the model nicely.

Only approved, switched-on tasks are offered. Destructive tasks, such as delete or cancel, are off by default.
Required steps, such as OTP or identity checks, can't be skipped.
Tasks that can't be undone need an explicit confirmation before the final submit.
Requests go only to the endpoints written in the approved manifest.

Generated pages are checked before they're shown: known components only, real endpoints only.
Answers must cite your content, and code comes only from your docs.
If anything fails, the visitor goes to your site's own page for that task.

The model sees what the visitor asked, never their form data.
Details remembered to pre-fill other forms stay in that browser tab, and visitors can clear them.
Your model key stays on your server.

The video on the website (public/media/intent0.mp4 / .webm) is made from a real recording of intent0 on the example site, placed into animated scenes.
Run the example site and intent0 next to it (see examples/city-services/README.md), without a model key.
Record the footage (Chrome DevTools screencast frames + timestamps): node record.mjs ./raw (needs the playwright package and Chromium)
Serve this folder and render the scenes frame by frame at 30 fps: python3 -m http.server 8099 --bind 127.0.0.1 then node render.mjs ./frames all (stills renders a few preview frames)
Encode:
compose.html holds the script and timing of every scene. The agent scene shows a real tools/call result from the example site.

code.code:
ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i frames/%05d.jpg -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 22 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart intent0.mp4
   ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i frames/%05d.jpg -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 36 -row-mt 1 intent0.webm
   ffmpeg -i frames/00400.jpg -q:v 3 -vf scale=1600:-1 poster.jpg
